topic: What happens if you sleep in your contact lenses?
title: What Happens If You Sleep In Your Contacts?
sources: Wikipedia, 'Cornea' (accessed 2026-11-16): the healthy cornea has no blood vessels; oxygen dissolves in tears and diffuses through the cornea; corneal neovascularization is 'excessive ingrowth of blood vessels ... caused by deprivation of oxygen from the air'; corneal ulcer involves disruption of the epithelial layer with involvement of the stroma

Wikipedia, 'Keratitis' (accessed 2026-11-16): in contact lens wearers ~90% of infectious keratitis cases are bacterial, of which Pseudomonas aeruginosa is responsible for ~40%; P. aeruginosa 'produces enzymes that can digest the cornea'; infectious keratitis 'can progress rapidly'; risk practices include wearing lenses overnight or in the shower, not replacing cases, storing lenses in tap water; complications include corneal scarring, perforation, loss of the eye

Wikipedia, 'Acanthamoeba keratitis' (accessed 2026-11-16): rare (~100 US cases/yr); 'nearly always associated with soft contact lens use'; Austrian 20-yr study: 89% of infected patients were contact lens wearers, 19% required a corneal transplant; amoeba from tap water/contaminated solution survives between lens and eye; cysts hard to eradicate

lines.text: What happens if you sleep in your contact lenses?
Your cornea has no blood vessels.
It gets its oxygen straight from the air.
A lens plus a closed eyelid cuts that supply off.
lines.caps: A *lens | plus a *closed eyelid | cuts that *off

lines.text: Micro-tears open in the starved cornea.
Their enzymes digest the cornea, fast.
By morning, a red, painful ulcer.
In rare cases, a scar or a corneal transplant.
So take your lenses out before bed, every time.
And never let them touch tap water.
